```{python}
#| include: false
# Data comes from reading/data/reading.csv, written by update_reading.py
# from a StoryGraph export. Only read and currently-reading books are kept.
import html
import sys
from pathlib import Path

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import pandas as pd

sys.path.insert(0, str(next(p for p in Path.cwd().resolve().parents
                            if (p / "_quarto.yml").exists())))
import site_style as ss
ss.apply()

books = pd.read_csv("data/reading.csv")
books["finished"] = pd.to_datetime(books["Last Date Read"], format="%Y/%m/%d", errors="coerce")
# A few books only have a year recorded; they still count toward that year.
books["year"] = pd.to_numeric(books["Last Date Read"].str[:4], errors="coerce")
books["rating"] = pd.to_numeric(books["Star Rating"], errors="coerce")
books["times_read"] = pd.to_numeric(books["Read Count"], errors="coerce").fillna(1).astype(int)

read = books[books["Read Status"] == "read"]
current = books[books["Read Status"] == "currently-reading"]
dated = read.dropna(subset=["year"])
per_year = dated.groupby(dated["year"].astype(int)).size()

this_year = pd.Timestamp.today().year
so_far = int(per_year.get(this_year, 0))
average = read["rating"].mean()
```

I keep track of what I read on [StoryGraph](https://app.thestorygraph.com/). This page is built from that record: `{python} len(read)` books finished so far, `{python} so_far` of them in `{python} this_year`, with an average rating of `{python} f"{average:.2f}"` out of 5.

## By the Numbers

```{python}
#| label: fig-books-per-year
#| fig-cap: "Books finished each calendar year."
years = per_year.index.astype(int)
colors = [ss.BRICK] * len(years)

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6.8, 3.4))
bars = ax.bar(years, per_year.values, width=0.6, color=colors)
bars[-1].set_alpha(0.45) if years[-1] == this_year else None
for y, n in zip(years, per_year.values):
    label = f"{n} so far" if y == this_year else f"{n}"
    ax.text(y, n + 1.5, label, ha="center", va="bottom", fontsize=10.5, color=ss.MUTED)
ax.set_xticks(list(years))
ax.set_ylim(0, per_year.max() * 1.2)
ss.titles(fig, "Books finished each year", "From my StoryGraph library", y=0.95)
plt.show()
```

```{python}
#| label: fig-ratings
#| fig-cap: "My star ratings, grouped to the nearest half star."
halves = (read["rating"].dropna() * 2).round() / 2
counts = halves.value_counts().reindex([x / 2 for x in range(2, 11)], fill_value=0)

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6.8, 3.2))
ax.bar(counts.index, counts.values, width=0.38, color=ss.INDIGO)
ax.set_xticks(list(counts.index), [f"{x:g}" for x in counts.index])
ss.axis_heading(ax, "Books")
ss.titles(fig, f"My most common rating is {counts.idxmax():g} stars",
          f"{int(counts.sum())} rated books; average {average:.2f}", y=0.97)
plt.show()
```

## Books Read

```{python}
#| output: asis
def table(rows):
    """One year's books as an HTML table, newest first."""
    out = ['<table class="table table-sm reading-table"><thead><tr>'
           '<th>Title</th><th>Author</th><th>Finished</th><th>Rating</th></tr></thead><tbody>']
    for _, b in rows.iterrows():
        title = html.escape(b["Title"])
        if b["times_read"] > 1:
            title += f' <span class="reading-reread">read {b["times_read"]}×</span>'
        finished = b["finished"].strftime("%b %-d") if pd.notna(b["finished"]) else ""
        rating = f'{b["rating"]:g} ★' if pd.notna(b["rating"]) else ""
        out.append(f"<tr><td>{title}</td><td>{html.escape(b['Authors'])}</td>"
                   f"<td>{finished}</td><td>{rating}</td></tr>")
    out.append("</tbody></table>")
    return "\n".join(out)


sections = [(str(y), dated[dated["year"] == y].sort_values("finished", ascending=False))
            for y in sorted(per_year.index.astype(int), reverse=True)]
undated = read[read["year"].isna()].sort_values("Title")
if len(undated):
    sections.append(("Date not recorded", undated))

print("```{=html}")
for i, (name, rows) in enumerate(sections):
    is_open = " open" if i == 0 else ""
    print(f'<details class="collapsible-section"{is_open}>')
    print(f"<summary><h3>{name} <small>· {len(rows)} books</small></h3></summary>")
    print(table(rows))
    print("</details>")
print("```")
```
